report:
Reviewed the complete canonical_ownership claim, all four associated implementation files, both associated test entries, and captured inspection.sage plus the live-host helper and fixture manifest/source. This is source inspection; I did not execute the behavioral test or repeat centrally run suites. No source changes were made.

The local implementation in src/inspector.rs separates labels from paths: symbol_identity_parts constructs kind-prefixed, escaped named segments, canonical_children adds occurrence suffixes for repeated bases, and walk_symbols/find_local_reference construct ownership chains. resolve_local_symbol replays each segment against current owned children, so named identity depends on ownership/name rather than sibling location or product detail. Selection returns symbol-not-found when replay fails. This supports unrelated/detail edits and reconstruction while making old rename/move/delete/forged paths fail, subject to the explicit anonymous qualification. Anonymous segments use hashes and duplicate occurrence numbers: within a revision repeated representations are distinguished; these are deliberately not persistent entity IDs, and indistinguishable anonymous changes or descendant links can resolve differently. No stronger anonymous persistence guarantee is inferred.

External references are constructed from backend canonical_def_path, stable crate disambiguator, kind/name/disambiguator segments and a separate label. resolve_external_path validates the crate and each actual child prefix instead of treating client text as a definition ID. The associated rustc bridge implementation walks definition ownership and includes unnamed segments only for canonical navigation; its structured path variant omits them. This separation is relevant to the navigation-versus-semantic-identity qualification, but is not treated as proof of the entire import-route equivalence oracle.

Anonymous imports specifically hash each token-rendered import path, binding-kind discriminant, and named binding text. They do not hash the import span or database-local handles. The associated Path ToTokens implementation renders names/anchors/segments from the stash; the associated StringSink concatenates their textual tokens. These essential helpers are associated, rather than relying on the inspector marker alone. The ordinary anonymous_use_paths_survive_sibling_reordering test obtains two use-item paths and source products, reverses sibling imports, and asserts each saved path still returns its exact original source. It reconstructs a fresh host, reverses modules/imports, and repeats exact source equality. The captured run_sage_host_with helper creates a new SageHost for each callback; the manifest identifies the real fixture root. Thus this test provides concrete evidence for the new position/handle-independent anonymous import behavior, not merely an assertion that navigation succeeds.

The separate TODO entry explicitly retains incomplete association and review of the broader ownership-path evidence: local associated/generated ownership, named stability and failure scenarios, external parent/children and crate disambiguation, and the full exact oracle proving navigation detail does not contaminate semantic identity. Its prerequisite is to associate and review those complete assertion sets. I accept this as an honest visible deferral, not as executable coverage or proof that every claim scenario is complete. In particular the ordinary import regression does not establish all named rename/move/deletion failures, all binding kinds, anonymous descendant edge cases, or route-equivalent semantic identity. Those remain within the stated broader evidence deferral. All entries and claim qualifications are accounted for without weakening the claim or upgrading the TODO to completion. No concrete defect was identified in the reviewed behavior and no edits are requested.
